analysis.detail: GnuPG binary package. GnuPG is installed for build-time package signature verification only; not invoked at runtime by Liquibase.

vulnerabilities.description: GnuPG can be made to spin on a relatively small input by (for example) crafting a public key with thousands of signatures attached, compressed down to just a few KB.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. GnuPG is not invoked at container runtime.

ratings.justification: No gpg/gnupg/dirmngr invocation exists anywhere in this image's runtime.

analysis.detail: GnuPG can be made to spin/consume excessive CPU on a relatively small input, such as a crafted public key with thousands of signatures compressed into a few KB (explicit upstream won't-fix). No gpg/gnupg/dirmngr invocation exists anywhere in this image's runtime.

vulnerabilities.description: gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside the selected extraction directory. The write is limited by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not have this risk.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase never runs gpgtar.

ratings.justification: CNA score; NVD had not yet published its own score at assessment time.
gpgtar is never run in the Liquibase image.

analysis.detail: The file overwrite affects gpgtar when it extracts an untrusted archive with --directory into a directory that contains a pre-existing symlink. GnuPG is present in the liquibase/liquibase-secure 6.0.3 image only as a dependency of apt. Liquibase never runs gpgtar or any other GnuPG tool; the image entrypoint runs Liquibase, and runs another program only when the user passes it as the container command. Ubuntu rates the issue low priority.
